question: Who was the author of ‘The Great Indian Novel’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashi Tharoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shashi Tharoor is a renowned Indian author and politician.
 
• He is known for his eloquent writing style and deep insights into Indian history and politics.
 
• "The Great Indian Novel" is a satirical novel by Shashi Tharoor that retells the Mahabharata through the context of the Indian independence movement and the early years of the Republic of India.
 
• Tharoor has won numerous literary awards and has been a significant figure in Indian literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Great Indian Novel**

 
 
• The novel's title is a play on the title of the Indian epic, the Mahabharata, with "great" also referring to the British imperial name for India.
 
• The novel covers the period from the British Raj and the Indian Independence Movement to the early years of the Indian Republic.
 
• It is structured in 18 books, modeled after the 18 books of the Mahabharata, and each book is narrated by a character called Ved Vyas, which is also a nod to the traditional author of the Mahabharata.
 
• The narrative intertwines historical and mythological events, blending real historical figures with fictional characters, providing a satirical and critical perspective on the Indian political landscape.
 
 
 
• **Shashi Tharoor**
 
 
• Shashi Tharoor is an Indian politician, diplomat, and author, currently serving as a Member of Parliament for Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
 
• He has previously served as an Under-Secretary-General at the United Nations.
 
• Tharoor has written numerous books, both fiction and non-fiction, including "Inglorious Empire", "The Paradoxical Prime Minister", and "Why I Am a Hindu".
 
• He is known for his erudite and articulate speeches and writings, often addressing complex issues of Indian history, culture, and politics.
